acceptanceCriteria: A sanctioned operator recovery path for a quarantined dispatch reader marker is specified in the CAL spec with numbered requirements, failure modes and rollback
The recovery records quiescence evidence and never deletes the marker without it
A test exercises HOLD, refused restart, recovery, then successful restart
body: Found in the independent review of #464 (dispatch reader lifecycle, branch codex/dispatch-464-cancel, source d1b6f13d, internal/tasks/dispatch/reader.go). When a dispatcher Close takes the HOLD/UNKNOWN exception, the persisted marker `reader-lifecycle.json` (profile taskman-dispatch-reader-lifecycle/0, lifecycle UNKNOWN) is preserved and every later start refuses with QUIESCENCE_UNPROVED via checkReaderQuarantine. The code and CAL S11 text say neither the record nor the marker grants recovery authority, and that downgrading or removing the marker does not establish containment, but no sanctioned operator path exists to prove quiescence and lift the quarantine. Actual: the only way forward is manual deletion of the marker, which the contract says proves nothing. Expected: an explicit, evidence-bound operator recovery command (or documented procedure) that records the quiescence proof, and a test that exercises HOLD -> recovery -> restart. Reviewer severity MED; not a regression introduced by #464, which deliberately grants no recovery authority.
title: corvint-tasks dispatch: no operator recovery path after a reader HOLD quarantine
